import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {'Company': ['Apple', 'Microsoft', 'Alphabet', 'Amazon', 'Meta', 'NVIDIA', 'Samsung', 'TSMC', 'Oracle', 'Salesforce'],
        'Revenue_B': [395, 227, 307, 575, 135, 61, 200, 75, 53, 35]}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_sorted = df.sort_values('Revenue_B', ascending=True)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
plt.barh(df_sorted['Company'], df_sorted['Revenue_B'])
plt.xlabel('Revenue (Billions USD)')
plt.title('Top 10 Tech Companies by Revenue')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/tmp/autogen_chart.png')
print('Chart saved to /tmp/autogen_chart.png')

# ASCII bar chart fallback
companies = [('Amazon', 575), ('Apple', 395), ('Alphabet', 307), ('Microsoft', 227), ('Samsung', 200), ('Meta', 135), ('TSMC', 75), ('NVIDIA', 61), ('Oracle', 53), ('Salesforce', 35)]
max_rev = max(r for _, r in companies)
for name, rev in companies:
    bar = '#' * int(rev / max_rev * 40)
    print(f'{name:12s} | {bar} ${rev}B')
